quarterly_data.signal: Duke Energy Carolinas' 2025 North Carolina rate case: on July 17, 2026 it filed a Comprehensive Revenue Requirement Settlement with the Public Staff and other intervenors resolving all remaining revenue requirement issues - a 9.8% ROE with a 53% equity component, a North Carolina retail rate base of approximately $25.7 billion for the historic base case, and approximately $3.8 billion of capital (NC retail allocation) in the multi-year rate plan (MYRP) with an annual MYRP refund mechanism. The stipulations result in a revised revenue requirement of $496 million over the two-year period, an average annual rate increase of 3.7% over two years (the initial filing requested approximately $1,002 million). The parties agree to support a separate proceeding to evaluate a large load tariff, intended to be completed before new rates take effect; the company will evaluate delaying its next base rate case filing until no earlier than November 1, 2028 if permitted to defer costs of the Commission-approved Person County CC1 and Marshall CTs. The settlement is subject to NCUC approval; DEC has requested Year 1 rates to be in effect no later than January 1, 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 9.8% ROE; rate base approximately $25.7 billion; MYRP capital approximately $3.8 billion; revenue requirement $496 million over two years
